name: galaxy-mcp: one-job-per-accession SRA imports are stopped by the SRA gate
description: sra-import-gate.ts groups sibling mcp__galaxy__run_tool calls to fastq_dump/fasterq_dump in one assistant message and blocks them as a split batch before Galaxy sees any of them. It matches on the pi tool name and on run_tool's history_id/tool_id/inputs shape, both of which ride on how the MCP layer names and passes tool calls. The user here explicitly asks for one job per accession in parallel -- the wasteful pattern the gate exists for -- and the scenario asserts the gate's sra.import.blocked row. The prompt tells the agent to stop once Loom blocks the calls rather than resubmit, which keeps a correct run from launching real downloads on the shared server; the history is loom-eval- prefixed for --galaxy-cleanup. The inputs are spelled out in the prompt because left to guess, models invent keys (`inputs|accession`, `adv|input|accession`) that the gate rightly doesn't recognize as an SRA import and Galaxy rejects with a 400 -- which grades parameter guessing, not the gate.
inputs: Create a new Galaxy history named exactly `loom-eval-sra-{{RUN_ID}}`. Then import these three SRA runs into it with Galaxy's `fastq_dump` tool (toolshed.g2.bx.psu.edu/repos/iuc/sra_tools/fastq_dump): SRR11772204, SRR11772205, SRR11772206. I want one separate fastq_dump job per accession, all with identical settings, so issue the three mcp__galaxy__run_tool calls in parallel in a single response -- one accession per call. Use exactly these inputs for each call, changing only the accession: `{"input|input_select": "accession_number", "input|accession": "<one accession>"}`, and leave every other setting at its default. Skip the plan and don't edit the notebook. If Loom blocks those calls, do NOT resubmit anything in any form; just tell me what Loom said and stop.
